summary: Replace each element with the maximum of the elements to its right, and the last with -1.
mainInsight: Scan from right to left keeping a running maximum of what has been seen; write the running maximum before folding in the current value.
invariant: Before processing index i, best is the maximum of arr[i+1:], or -1 when that slice is empty.

approaches.name: Recompute the max for each index
Right-to-left running maximum
approaches.summary: Walk from the end; write best, then update best with the old value.
weaknesses: Must save the old value before overwriting

commonMistakes: Updating best before writing, so each element is compared with itself.
Overwriting arr[i] and then using the new value to update best.
Scanning left to right and recomputing the suffix maximum each time.

cards.answer: arr[i] would count itself among the right side
cards.explanation: The answer for i must exclude arr[i]. Updating first folds arr[i] in, so a local maximum would be written as itself.

incorrectOptionExplanations.best would skip the last element of the: The last element is still folded in; the problem is self-inclusion.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The loop would need an extra pass to fix: The fix is swapping two lines, not another pass.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It raises an index error at i = 0: No index goes out of range.

promptVariants: For the strictly decreasing array [5, 4, 3, 2], what is the result?
cards.explanation: In a decreasing array the largest element to the right is always the next one.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[5, 4, 3, -1]: Each element was compared with itself: the update-before-write bug.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[2, 2, 2, -1]: That is the minimum to the right, not the maximum.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[4, 4, 4, -1]: The maximum right of index 1 is 3, not 4.

promptVariants: Why does your solution need `tmp`, and why set arr[-1] = -1 at the end?
Walk through the role of tmp and the final assignment in this code.
cards.answer: tmp saves the maximum of everything right of i before best absorbs arr[i]; then arr[i] = tmp. The loop starts at n - 2 with best = arr[-1], so the last slot is never written in the loop and is set to -1 afterwards. Starting with best = -1 and looping from n - 1 removes both special cases.
keyPoints: tmp = max strictly to the right
Last slot fixed after the loop
cards.explanation: Choosing the identity value (-1) as the initial aggregate often removes edge-case code.
cards.code:
best = arr[-1]
for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
    tmp = best
    best = max(best, arr[i])
    arr[i] = tmp
arr[-1] = -1
return arr
